item.title: Version 0.9
item.description:
Transcripts no longer get stuck in the wrong language

  • The big fix. If Seal misheard your first few words as another language, it used to stay stuck there for the rest of the meeting — and quietly discard the lines it had got right. In one 64-minute English lesson, most of one speaker's side came out as Cyrillic. Now the two sides of a call check each other: when the person you are talking to is clearly speaking one language, Seal reconsiders instead of digging in.
  • Genuinely bilingual calls are unaffected. A speaker who has really established their own language keeps it — only a weakly supported guess can be overruled.
  • Each recording now keeps a small diagnostic log beside it, so a transcript that still comes out wrong can be explained instead of guessed at. Like everything else in Seal, it never leaves your Mac.

item.title: Version 0.8
item.description:
Recording no longer disturbs your Mac's audio playback

  • The deeper fix for Bluetooth headphones. 0.7 stopped Seal from using the headset's microphone, but the system-audio capturer itself could still make playback lag, go silent, or disconnect the headset. Seal now captures the Mac's audio through a lighter mechanism that leaves the output device completely untouched.
  • One new permission, one old one retired. The first recording will ask to allow "System Audio Recording" — click Allow. The broader Screen Recording permission is no longer needed.
  • Sessions that start on music no longer open with stray "Music"/"Музика" lines.

item.title: Version 0.7
item.description:
Your headphones keep full audio quality while recording

  • Recording with AirPods (or any Bluetooth headset) no longer ruins playback. Starting a recording used to switch the headset into its low-quality call mode — sound became muffled, choppy, or cut out until the recording stopped. Seal now records from a wired microphone instead (the Mac's built-in mic, or a display microphone), so the headset stays in full-quality music mode. A caption shows which mic is in use.
  • On a Mac with no wired microphone, Seal keeps the headset mic and says playback quality may drop — no more mystery.

item.title: Version 0.6
item.description:
Meeting pages no longer share state with each other

  • "Generating notes" showed on every meeting, not just the one generating. Each AI job (Generate notes, Reshape, Improve transcript, Draft follow-up, Extract actions) now belongs to the meeting it was started for and shows progress only there.
  • Results always land on the right meeting — a finished generation can no longer drop its text into whichever meeting was open, and a title or tag edited while the model worked is no longer reverted when it finishes.
  • Heavy AI jobs no longer stack — one at a time.

item.title: Version 0.5
item.description:
Transcription no longer silently stops mid-meeting

  • A rare glitch could freeze one side of the transcript — audio kept being captured, but no new lines appeared for that speaker until the end of the meeting. The engine's internal jobs now run strictly one at a time, and each has a time limit: if anything ever gets stuck again, Seal abandons that one sentence and keeps going. Worst case changed from "rest of the meeting lost" to "one sentence lost."
  • Two more guards against invented lines in the opening seconds of a recording, before the meeting's language has settled.

If an earlier meeting was affected, its audio is saved — open it and use "Improve transcript" to recover the full text.

item.title: Version 0.4
item.description:
Removes the last way a foreign word could sneak in

  • No more invented words in the wrong alphabet — anywhere in a meeting. After a recording went quiet (a video ended, everyone stopped talking), background noise could still appear as a word like "Дякую." even in an all-English session. A short line written in an alphabet that doesn't match its own language is now recognized as noise and dropped, at any point in a meeting. Real short answers and genuine language switches are untouched.

item.title: Version 0.3
item.description:
Fixes meetings coming out nearly empty on English calls

  • Whole meetings are no longer lost to a language mix-up. Seal read its language detector's answer backwards, so an English call could be treated as "certainly Ukrainian" — the transcript then filtered itself down to a handful of lines, or filled with Cyrillic look-alikes of English words. Detection is now read correctly, and a line needs real evidence before it can pull the meeting toward another language.
  • No more invented words at the start of a recording. The meeting-join chime could appear as "Дякую!" or "you" before anyone spoke. Stock filler words are ignored until someone has actually said something — real greetings still come through.
  • "Improve transcript" fixed too — it had the same backwards reading and could redo an entire English meeting in the wrong language.
  • On Macs with less memory, lines from the very end of a meeting can no longer be silently lost while notes are being prepared.

item.title: Version 0.2
item.description:
Noticeably more accurate transcripts

  • No more Cyrillic in English recordings. Seal could invent Russian or Ukrainian words in places where nobody had actually spoken — in one English-only call, 17% of lines came back in the wrong alphabet. Silence is now read as silence.
  • Repetitive speech is kept. Saying similar phrases in a row, like reading out a list, no longer looks like a stuck decoder, so those words are no longer discarded.
  • Lines appear in the order they were spoken. A reply could previously show up above the remark it answered. Consecutive lines from the same speaker now join into one turn instead of being split at every short pause.

Seal also reports its real version number now, so this is the first release that can keep itself up to date automatically.
